ZRG Aspen Leadership Group is proud to partner with Ronald McDonald House Charities® of Southern California (RMHCSC) in their search for an Executive Director, Ronald McDonald House Los Angeles.


**ABOUT RMHCSC:**
  

For nearly 50 years, Ronald McDonald House Charities® of Southern California has kept families close when they need it most. They remove barriers and provide wrap\-around care so parents can focus on what matters most: their child. With a $20\+ million operating budget, the organization serves as a vital resource for families across Southern California, working to build a community where children and their families embrace life and healing with a sense of hope, enthusiasm, courage and joy.


RMHCSC expresses their mission through their programs, which include seven Ronald McDonald Houses in Bakersfield, Inland Empire, Long Beach, Los Angeles, Orange County, Pasadena, and Westside Los Angeles. The Chapter also operates two Ronald McDonald Family Rooms at CHOC Children's Hospital in Orange and CHOC Children's at Mission Hospital. RMHCSC is one of the only Ronald McDonald House Charities chapters across the world that operates a cost\-free, medically\-supervised camp for children with cancer and their families, Camp Ronald McDonald for Good Times.


The generosity of time, funds, and in\-kind services provided by the entire McDonald's community, including local owner\-operators and McDonald's vendors, have helped RMHC positively impact millions of children and their families since 1974\. Their support and community relations have also helped the Chapter expand its core programs and services throughout the world. Currently, McDonald'sprovides approximately 10\-15% of RMHCSC's annual budget. Although McDonald's is their largest corporate partner, RMHCSC is a nonprofit 501(c)(3\) corporation. RMHCSC relies on the support of the entire community to help achieve their goals worldwide.


**RONALD MCDONALD HOUSE LOS ANGELES**
  

Ronald McDonald House Los Angeles (LARMH) is a program of Ronald McDonald House Charities® of Southern California.


For over 45 years, the Ronald McDonald House Los Angeles has provided a “home away from home” to up to 75 families, 24 hours a day, 365 days a year. The program has an operating budget of $4\.2M and a capital loan from their last expansion effort of $3M. Since its chartering, LARMH has served more than 30,000 families from all states in the U.S. and more than 45 countries across the world.


They are conveniently located across from Children’s Hospital Los Angeles and nearby several other world\-class, Los Angeles\-area pediatric facilities. Families access private bedrooms, hot meals via the Meals of Love program, kitchens, exercise facilities, washers and dryers, play areas, and comprehensive family support services.

This is a unique opportunity for a visionary leader to guide one of the most recognized Ronald McDonald Houses in the world while helping shape the future of the largest Ronald McDonald House chapter in North America. As an integral member of the RMHCSC Leadership Team, the Executive Director, Ronald McDonald House Los Angeles will be responsible for providing leadership and management for Ronald McDonald House Los Angeles, as well as serving as a key member of the chapter’s executive leadership team.


Working in partnership with the Chief Executive Officer and the Program Board of Trustees, the Executive Director will ensure success in program management, budget and fiscal oversight, supervision of employees, resource development/fundraising, marketing, board development, and general non\-profit business operations.

For more than 45 years, Ronald McDonald House Los Angeles has been a place of comfort, hope, and healing for families whose children are receiving lifesaving medical care. Every day, families arrive carrying uncertainty, fear, and exhaustion. Every day, our team has the privilege of reminding them that they don't have to face their child's medical journey alone.


I've had the privilege of serving Ronald McDonald House Charities of Southern California for the past fifteen years, including the last five as Chief Executive Officer. In that time I’ve seen the incredible generosity of our community, including individuals, corporations, foundations, healthcare partners, volunteers, and community leaders who believe every family deserves to stay close to their child during a medical crisis. That generosity has allowed us to serve more families than ever before, and I believe the opportunity ahead is even greater.


As part of Ronald McDonald House, we're also part of a global movement advancing family centered care for millions of families around the world. Departmental Overview
  
  

The Office of the Vice Chancellor for Research (VCRO) has overall managerial responsibility for Berkeley's research enterprise. Within the VCRO, and under the Office of the Chief Innovation \& Entrepreneurship Officer, UC Berkeley's Life Sciences Entrepreneurship Center (LSEC) is a unique "center of centers" that fosters life sciences entrepreneurship by coordinating and building upon existing campus resources.
  
  

Position Summary
  
  

The Executive Director (ED) is responsible for running, scaling, and ensuring the long\-term sustainability of the Life Sciences Entrepreneurship Center (LSEC). Operating as a unique "center\-of\-centers," created in 2021, LSEC connects and catalyzes UC Berkeley's world\-class life sciences and entrepreneurship ecosystems\-including Berkeley SkyDeck, Bakar Labs, the Innovative Genomics Institute (IGI), the Bakar Fellows Program, the Molecular Therapeutics Institute, Berkeley Haas, and others.
  
  

The Executive Director operates with a high degree of autonomy and consensus\-building skill, managing complex, unprecedented collaborations across organizational boundaries. A prime example includes leading and coordinating high\-profile, multi\-entity initiatives like the Berkeley Bio Startup Showcase at the annual J.P. Morgan Healthcare Conference. This role requires a balance of high\-level external relationship management, fundraising, and board governance, paired with a disciplined, execution\-focused approach to managing and optimizing LSEC's established portfolio of academic and startup programs.
  
  

The Executive Director's mandate spans five core strategic and operational areas:

**Board Management:** Directly leads and engages LSEC's Board of Advisors and its broader network of industry experts, serving as the primary liaison to align board expertise with the center's goals.
  
**External Relationship Management:** Manages and generalizes external industry and donor relationships, ensuring LSEC complements rather than disrupts existing campus partnerships, while maximizing the mutual value generated for both the campus and external partners.
  
**Financial Model \& Sustainability:** Leads the transition of LSEC from its initial five\-year "term" startup capital toward a self\-sustaining financial model. The ED is responsible for identifying new capital pipelines, revenue models, and donor opportunities to fund high\-value, emerging initiatives.
  
**Academic Program Design \& Optimization:** Oversees the delivery, design, and iterative improvement of LSEC's programs. **About the Asian Cultural Council**

Headquartered in New York City, the Asian Cultural Council (ACC) is a leading nonprofit organization working to foster cultural exchange between Asia and the U.S. to advance international dialogue, mutual understanding, and respect. Individual fellowships and organizational grants are awarded to support research, study, and creative work by leaders practicing 16 disciplines in the arts and humanities in the U.S. and 25 countries and regions in Asia. Since its incorporation as a nonprofit in 1980, ACC has awarded more than $100 million in grants and has supported nearly 6,000 exchanges.

As a grantmaking and grant\-seeking organization, ACC raises funds from individuals, foundations, and corporate donors.

ACC has a current annual operating budget of approximately $4\.5 million. Revenue sources include charitable contributions, special events, a biennial gala, and investment returns. The organization has an endowment with a current market value of approximately $53 million. ACC staff in New York work closely with four affiliate offices in Hong Kong, Taipei, Tokyo, and Manila.

All ACC staff currently work in a hybrid environment (minimum of three days in\-office). The Director of Development and Communications will be expected to live within reasonable commuting distance to New York City for regular in\-person meetings with prospective donors, patrons, Trustees, and staff.

**Position Summary**

The Director of Development and Communications serves as a member of ACC's leadership team and is responsible for the strategic direction, management, and execution of the organization's comprehensive fundraising and communications program. The Director provides leadership for all aspects of philanthropic development, including annual giving, major gifts, foundation and corporate relations, donor stewardship, and development communications.

The Director is responsible for identifying and pursuing new funding opportunities while developing and implementing comprehensive cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship strategies to strengthen relationships with individual, corporate, foundation, and institutional donors.

The Director is accountable for raising a minimum of $2 million annually in philanthropic support (exclusive of annual trustee dues) and for increasing philanthropic revenue over time. The position also provides strategic leadership for ACC's $20 million endowment campaign, which has raised $11 million to date and is scheduled for completion in 2028, as well as other special fundraising initiatives.

The Director oversees the organization's communications strategy, ensuring consistent messaging, effective donor engagement, and increased visibility for ACC's mission and impact.

The Director fosters a culture of philanthropy throughout the organization by partnering with leadership, staff, and the Board of Trustees to integrate fundraising and donor stewardship into organizational priorities.

Reporting to the Executive Director, the Director of Development and Communications supervises a Development Specialist and a Marketing and Communications Officer. The Director also works closely with and supports Board members and serves on the Development Committee of the ACC Board.

**The following list of duties represents the core responsibilities of this position. Additional tasks, projects, or duties may be required as requested by the Executive Director.**

The University of Maryland Medicine philanthropy team is a joint initiative uniting the fundraising endeavors of the University of Maryland Medical Center and University of Maryland School of Medicine.
